purpose: Buttons enable users to trigger actions in applications, from submitting data to opening menus or toggling views. Available in 4 types: simple button, toggle button, segmented button, and menu button.
whenToUse: Use simple buttons for specific actions: Create/Edit/Save, Approve/Reject, Accept/Decline, OK/Cancel
Use toggle buttons in a toolbar to activate/deactivate an object or switch between states
Use segmented buttons in toolbar when user must select one option from a small group (e.g. Year/Month/Day)
Use menu button when you need a dropdown with more than one option
whenNotToUse: Don't use button to link to a different page or object — use Link instead
Don't use button for general navigation functions — use Home or Breadcrumbs
Don't use button to navigate a multi-step process — use Wizard
Don't use button for file upload — use Upload Set control
Don't use button when users must select from multiple related options — use RadioButton or CheckBox
doRules: One primary action (Emphasized style) per page maximum
Use Emphasized style for primary action in header/footer toolbar
Use Ghost (type=ghost) style for secondary actions in header/footer toolbar
Use Transparent style for negative path actions in header/footer toolbar
Use Accept/Reject semantic button styles for positive/negative actions; always text buttons
Use verb in imperative for button text (Save, Cancel, Edit)
Use counter badge to show number of affected items; attention badge to attract attention
dontRules: Do not use multiple Emphasized buttons per page — one primary action only
Do not use icon control for buttons — use the icon property of Button instead
Do not change text or icon of a toggle button when pressed — screen readers announce 'pressed' state
Do not use semantic button styles in content toolbars (tables, forms, charts)
Do not use icon-only buttons for business actions — only for generic standard icon metaphors
Do not use vague labels like 'OK', 'Click here', 'Submit' when specific text fits

layoutGuidance.placement: Primary action: right-aligned in header/footer toolbars. Negative path action: left side. In content toolbars: most important action highlighted, secondary/negative use Transparent style.
layoutGuidance.sizing: Grows to fit text. Fixed size causes truncation. Max width for menu button: 12rem (192px). Compact/Cozy supported.
layoutGuidance.spacing: 8px gap between buttons in toolbar. Counter badge: inside button (Compact) or top-right corner (Cozy).
layoutGuidance.alignment: Group related buttons. Separate destructive actions with spacing.

contentGuidance.labelLength: Short and meaningful. 1–3 words. Verb in imperative (Save, Cancel, Edit). Can add count in parentheses: Edit (3).
contentRules: Use imperative verb for all actions
Use standard action labels per UXC-015 terminology standard
Account for text up to 300% longer in other languages
Supports LTR and RTL reading directions

responsiveBehavior.XL: Full button with text and optional icon. Menu button triggers cascading dropdown.
responsiveBehavior.L: Full button with text and optional icon. Menu button triggers cascading dropdown.
responsiveBehavior.M: Full button. In responsive containers, button may move to another line.
responsiveBehavior.S: Menu button opens in full-screen dialog with Cancel footer. Items with submenus become navigable with Back button.

accessibilityGuidance.requirement: Enter and Space activate. Tab moves focus. Supports keyboard shortcuts via sap.ui.core.CommandExecution.
Visible focus indicator. States: regular, hover, pressed, focused, disabled.
Icon-only buttons MUST have tooltip + default accessibility text. Use app-specific text if icon name is not ideal.

incompatible: Inside Table cells at S viewport — use Link instead

exceptions: SAP Fiori Elements supports text-only buttons except in tables where inline actions can be icon or text (not both)
Within SAP S/4HANA, a button can contain either an icon or text (not both)
Toggle button stays pressed until pressed again — do not change text/icon in pressed state
types: Simple button: one action, text or icon
Toggle button: switches between two states; one always active
Segmented button: group of connected buttons, one selectable at a time
Standard menu button: opens menu on activation
Split menu button: text area triggers default action; arrow area opens dropdown menu
